title: IdP integration quirks, deterministic attribute mapping table, and automated SAML test suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a canonical, machine-readable IdP compatibility guide and deterministic attribute mapping table for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping; implement an automated SAML integration test suite (CI) that verifies RBAC v2 mappings and audit-log capture semantics.

Background: Multiple customer integrations and support tickets have revealed inconsistent IdP behavior across providers: NameID formats, group claim location (SAML attribute vs SCIM), large-group pagination, encrypted assertions, and unpredictable attribute name casing. These differences cause RBAC v2 mismatches and poor audit trails. This ticket defines the mapping rules we will ship in Console docs and the test harness that will run nightly in CI.

Acceptance criteria (AC):
1) A deterministic attribute mapping table (CSV/JSON) that lists for each IdP the canonical attribute names we will accept and the transformation order of precedence (NameID > email > sub > custom attributes), with examples.
2) A SAML test harness with 20+ test vectors covering: NameID formats (persistent, transient, email), signed-only vs signed-and-encrypted assertions, group delivery (attribute, MultiValued attribute, SCIM fallback), case-insensitive attribute names, and uncommon encodings. Harness must run in GitHub Actions and report pass/fail per provider.
3) RBAC v2 mapping unit tests validating: role precedence rules, group-to-role mapping logic, and fallback account creation behavior.
4) Audit logging spec and sample log lines showing captured raw assertion (truncated), normalized attributes, mapping decisions, and mapping source (e.g., "groups_from": "attribute:MemberOf"). Logs must be schema-compatible with our observability pipeline.
5) Console docs PR and Confluence spec merged; GitHub PR merging test harness code.

Proposed deterministic mapping table (summary):
- preferred_user_id: NameID (Format: persistent) -> fallback email -> fallback sub (UUID).
- email: SAML attribute keys accepted (Email, emailAddress, mail, user.email) case-insensitive.
- username: Prefer attribute 'eduPersonPrincipalName' then 'username' -> if missing derive from email local-part.
- groups: attribute keys accepted (Groups, group, memberOf) OR SCIM group sync. If both present, prefer attribute list (explicit SAML) and treat SCIM groups as additive.
- role: attribute 'role', 'appRole', or mapping via group_to_role table.

Notes on provider quirks (summary):
- Okta: often places roles in app-specific "appRole" attribute; test vector includes app user profile attribute maps. Okta sometimes returns NameID as 'email' format even when persistent requested.
- Azure AD: returns groups as Opaque Object IDs when group claims are enabled; requires Graph call to expand IDs to names for mapping if customer uses group names.
- Google Workspace: tends to use 'memberOf' and lowercased attribute names; also supports SAML encrypted assertions inconsistently across admin consoles.
- Ping: custom attribute name prefixes and group pagination; we observed truncated attribute lists for >100 groups in SAML responses — requires SCIM sync recommendation.

Deliverables:
- mapping-table.json (machine-readable) + mapping-table.csv (human) in repo.
- samples/ directory with SAML XML test vectors named by provider and case (e.g., samples/okta-nameid-persistent.xml).
- tests/integration/saml_harness/ with GitHub Actions workflow saml-compat-ci.yml.
- console docs PR pointing to Confluence spec and sample logs.

Out-of-scope: SCIM implementation work (SCIM edge cases will be covered as test expectations but SCIM sync changes are separate tickets).
